stories.headline: All election guarantees fulfilled, says Arvind Kejriwal; Opposition slams AAP of misusing public resources
stories.title: All election guarantees fulfilled, says Arvind Kejriwal; Opposition slams AAP of misusing public resources
stories.summary: The Opposition parties accuse AAP of misusing Punjab’s public resources to organise a party event while the State grapples with a mounting financial crisis
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ahead of the Assembly elections in Punjab, due in early 2027, Aam Aadmi Party’s national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) urged women to persuade the men in their families to vote for the AAP.

He was speaking at a rally in Moga on the party’s foundation day, where he highlighted the ₹1,000 financial assistance provided by the AAP Government to help women deal with inflation, taking a dig at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Government at the Centre.
The Opposition parties, meanwhile, targeted the AAP, accusing it of misusing Punjab’s public resources to organise a party event while the State grapples with a mounting financial crisis.

Mr. Kejriwal claimed that the AAP had fulfilled all its election guarantees within five years, adding that the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP had announced that they would discontinue the AAP Government’s existing schemes if voted to power.
“I am standing before people of Punjab today because my ‘Chota Bhai’, Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann, has fulfilled all of Kejriwal’s guarantees.
We promised free electricity and people are getting free electricity.
We promised to organise ‘tirth yatra,’ and now devotees are going on the ‘yatra.’ We promised to open Aam Aadmi Clinics and now people are receiving great treatment.
We promised free treatment, and everyone has been provided with a health insurance card worth ₹10 lakh,” he said.
The Smart Ration Card Scheme to extend food security benefits to 10 lakh beneficiaries was also launched at the event.

Leader of the Opposition in the Punjab Assembly Partap Singh Bajwa alleged that the Government machinery, including State-owned buses, administrative resources and police personnel were deployed for a political function at the expense of the public exchequer.
“Before calling it a ‘Khushhaal Rally’, the AAP must answer a fundamental question: has Punjab actually become prosperous under its rule?
When the State is drowning in debt, why is public money being spent on a party celebration?

stories.headline: UP BJP MLA Om Kumar's assembly election cancelled over nomination defects
stories.title: UP BJP MLA Om Kumar's assembly election cancelled over nomination defects
stories.summary: UP BJP MLA Om Kumar's assembly election cancelled over nomination defects
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Allahabad High Court set aside BJP MLA Om Kumar's Nehtaur election over a defective nomination affidavit.
The ruling permits limited Assembly participation for 15 days but bars voting and monetary benefits.

The Allahabad High Court on Thursday set aside the election of BJP MLA Om Kumar from the Nehtaur Assembly constituency in Uttar Pradesh's Bijnor district over defects in his nomination papers, while granting him a 15-day limited stay on the operation of the order.
Kumar had won the Scheduled Caste-reserved constituency in the 2022 Assembly elections by defeating Rashtriya Lok Dal candidate Munshi Ram by a margin of 258 votes.

Justice Salil Kumar Rai partly allowed an election petition filed by Munshi Ram but permitted Kumar to represent his constituency and participate in Assembly debates, if any, during the 15-day period.

"It is directed that for a period of fifteen days counted from today, the respondent Om Kumar shall be entitled to represent the electorate of his constituency and to participate in the debates of the Vidhan Sabha, if any, held during the period of fifteen days," the court said.
However, Kumar will not be allowed to vote in the Assembly or any of its committees during this period.
He will also not be entitled to any monetary benefits as an MLA.
The court held that Kumar's affidavit in Form 26 contained a substantial defect, warranting the rejection of his nomination under Sections 36(2) and 36(4) of the Representation of the People Act.
"His nomination paper was therefore improperly accepted by the returning officer and the improper acceptance of the nomination materially affected the result of his election," the court said.
The court, however, rejected Munshi Ram's allegations of irregularities in vote counting.

It held that he had failed to establish any illegality or irregularity in the counting of VVPAT slips from polling booths 44, 54, 180 and 234, or that any such irregularity had materially affected the election result.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill 8 Palestinians in Gaza, and other Mideast news
stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 8 Palestinians in Gaza, and other Mideast news
stories.summary: Dubai, Nov 26: Israeli strikes in Gaza overnight killed eight Palestinians, hospital officials there said, while a British military monitor said a tanker reported an explosion near it in the Persian Gulf west of Dubai. In Yemen, overnight strikes were reported in Sanaa, the capital controlled by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels. Here is the latest news from the Middle East on Thursday. Read our full coverage here. Israeli strikes kill eight people in Gaza Three Israeli strikes overnight into Thursday killed eight Palestinians in Gaza City and Central Gaza, according to health officials at Shifa hospital and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital, where the casualties were taken. A strike on a residential apartment in Deir Al-Balah City in central Gaza killed a man and his wife, health officials said. Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement that the military killed Khaled Abu Nada, who oversaw economic and education affairs for Hamas in Gaza, in the overnight strike. Two other strikes in Gaza City killed three people each, according to the Shifa hospital. Israel's military said that one of the strikes targeted three militants without elaborating, and did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the other strike. The overnight casualties are the latest in Gaza, where near-daily Israeli fire and airstrikes have persisted more than a year after a ceasefire deal was reached between Israel and Hamas. At least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed in more than three years of war in Gaza, according to the territory's health ministry. The ministry, which is part of the Hamas-led government, maintains casualty records that are seen as generally reliable but do not offer a breakdown of civilians and militants. Strikes reported in Yemen's rebel-held capital of Sanaa Iran-backed Houthi rebel media reported that strikes were carried out overnight into Thursday on Yemen's rebel-held capital of Sanaa. Houthi-controlled al-Masirah TV blamed the attacks on Saudi Arabia. The Associated Press couldn't independently verify these claims. Two residents, one in the south and one in the north of the city, said they heard explosions overnight. Khalil al-Makhlafi, who lives in the southern part of Sanaa, said his home is located near military camps, in an area where explosions are frequent. “We have to endure these sounds every now and then, and they have health implications for our kids,” al-Makhlafi said. The second resident, Randa al-Mahwiti, reported hearing explosions in the northern part of Sanaa. Yemen's humanitarian crisis is deepening Leaders from the United Nations and an international organisation took part in rare visits to war-torn Yemen, warning donors and the media are ignoring the worsening humanitarian crisis. Tom Fletcher, the UN humanitarian chief, warned that hunger is affecting millions of people. Jan Egeland, secretary general of the Norwegian Refugee Council, said in a separate visit this week that millions of people in northern Yemen are relying on just a handful of “overstretched and underfunded" national and international aid groups. He called on all of the sides to protect civilians and allow humanitarian aid. The number of people displaced in Yemen has reached 360,000 since the conflict escalated in August, according to UN figures, as fighting continues unabated across parts of the country between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed government forces. Tanker reports explosion in waters west of Dubai A British military monitor, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, said early Thursday that the captain of a tanker located 93 kilometres (58 miles) west of Dubai reported an explosion caused by “an unknown projectile in close proximity to the tanker” overnight. The UKMTO said no damage to the tanker was reported, and all crew were safe and accounted for. There has been an increase recently of incidents involving commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waters. The strategic waterway at the mouth of the Persian Gulf, through which about a fifth of the world's traded oil and natural gas passed before the Iran war, has been effectively shut by Iran's attacks on shipping since the start of the war in February. October saw the highest number of reported attacks on commercial shipping since March, during the war's opening weeks, according to the UKMTO. The organization has also noted that some ships have been reluctant to report incidents. Separately, Jordan's Foreign Ministry said the body of a Jordanian crew member reported missing after an attack on his vessel in the Strait of Hormuz had been recovered. The Nov. 17 attack wounded 11 other crew members, who were forced to abandon ship, according to the vessel's owner, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company. FlyDubai resumes ticket sales for direct flights between Israel and Dubai FlyDubai has resumed selling tickets for direct flights between Israel and Dubai after an axe-wielding pilot attempted to seize control of a plane in October and crash it into Israel's main airport. Passengers overpowered the pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, and the plane landed in Saudi Arabia. Israel suspended direct flights to Dubai after the attack while it reviewed security procedures, including how the pilot, an Omani national, had been allowed to fly to Tel Aviv despite Israel and Oman having no diplomatic relations. Earlier this week, Israel's Transportation Ministry said FlyDubai's direct flights could resume subject to approval from Israeli security services, following a delegation's visit to the United Arab Emirates. Israel's domestic and foreign intelligence services declined to comment on whether approval had been granted. Tickets are now on sale for flights beginning Dec. 3. (AP)

stories.headline: SC seeks census SOPs from Centre, Directorate of Census Operations
stories.title: SC seeks census SOPs from Centre, Directorate of Census Operations
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Centre and the Directorate of Census Operations to place on record the standard operating procedures governing the conduct of the census within a week. This would include the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submission made by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that she would apprise the court of the relevant SOPs. The bench asked the law officer to provide the details within a week. In its order dated October 12, the bench had requested the solicitor general to place on record the census SOPs being followed. It also directed that a complete set of the paper book be provided to the advocate-on-record for the Centre and the office of the solicitor general. A plea by Aakash Goel raised concerns over the methodology and safeguards for collecting and verifying

stories.headline: India’s kharif foodgrains estimate 5% lower on weather woes
stories.title: India’s kharif foodgrains estimate 5% lower on weather woes
stories.summary: Rice output pegged 2.3% lower as Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said farmers had to face challenges of lower rainfall, gap in spells of rain and damages due to cyclone and floods
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India’s kharif foodgrains output in the 2026-27 season has been estimated lower by 5.1 per cent at 167.14 million tonnes (mt) from 176.04 mt a year ago.
Rice production is pegged 2.3 per cent lower at 121.91 mt from 124.76 mt.

Releasing the first advance estimates of crop output, Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that despite the challenges due to deficient monsoon, Indian farmers have produced higher than the last five years’ average.

Admitting that the current year’s production has been pegged lower due to lower acreage, less rainfall, wide gap between rain spell and damage from cyclones and floods, he said still the country has sufficient foodgrains in stocks and the marginal fall in rice production willnot have any impact.
Asked about high prices of pulses and oilseeds which have adversely affected consumers, he said: “Most of the crops are selling either at their minimum support prices (MSPs) or higher levels.
Let farmers also get some good prices.
The government is also taking care of interests of the consumers.”

stories.headline: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan in murder case
stories.title: Supreme Court quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan in murder case
stories.summary: The apex court says Article 21 is not a “one-sided guarantee, equally encompasses victims, society at large
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) quashed the premature release of former MP Anand Mohan, who was serving life term in the 1994 murder case of then Gopalganj district magistrate G. Krishnaiah.

A Bench headed by Justice Dipankar Datta said the fundamental right to life under Article 21 was not exclusively meant for the convict alone, but also encompasses the rights of the victims, their families and the society at large.
“Article 21 cannot be a one-sided guarantee,” Justice Datta, who pronounced the judgment, read from its operative part.
The Court set aside the Bihar government’s notification on remission policy as arbitrary, and found the sudden departure from the pre-existing policy indefensible and unreasonable.
The Court said the sole criterion for a premature release policy cannot be that a convict “showed signs of reform”.
Quashing the release of Mohan, the Court directed the State to ensure his surrender in one month.
The Court directed that any future attempt for remission in this case must ensure that Uma Krishnaiah, the wife of the slain officer, was heard.
During the hearing, the Court had wondered how the murder of a public servant on duty was not considered the rarest of rare case.
In this case, Mohan was awarded death penalty on October 5, 2007 by the trial court, which was commuted to rigorous life imprisonment by the Patna High Court on December 10, 2008.
The High Court order was confirmed by the apex court in July 2012.
Senior advocate Sidharth Luthra, for the wife, had argued that the State Remission Board had not considered all the relevant aspects.
“It is a case where this lady is battling against the travesty of justice,” Mr. Luthra had submitted before the court had reserved the case for judgment.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets four-month deadline for FSSAI to finalise stricter food labelling norms
stories.title: Supreme Court sets four-month deadline for FSSAI to finalise stricter food labelling norms
stories.summary: The court has asked FSSAI to treat ‘total sugars’ and ‘saturated fat’, rather than ‘added sugar’ and ‘added fat’, alongside salt, as the nutrients of concern
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Observing that the right to health casts an obligation on the state to regulate industry practices detrimental to public health, the Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to formulate a single-phase front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) regime mandating prominent red warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, saturated fat or salt.
The court also asked the regulator to “strictly adhere” to the four-month deadline for finalising the draft regulations.

The judgment is the culmination of a series of interventions by a Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran in a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by the Kerala-based NGO 3S and Our Health Society seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fat.

“The population’s exposure to harmful substances must be controlled, their consumption must be discouraged, and consumers must be protected from practices detrimental to health used by the food businesses.
Preventive measures that are most effective must therefore be undertaken in an effort to respect, protect and guarantee the right to health,” the Bench said.

In a direction that will require the FSSAI to recalibrate the thresholds for mandatory warning labels, the Bench asked the regulator to treat “total sugars” and “saturated fat”, rather than “added sugar” and “added fat”, alongside salt, as the nutrients of concern, in keeping with the regulatory consensus that preceded the 2024 Dietary Guidelines for Indians (DGI).
The Bench cautioned that the thresholds must be neither too high nor too low.

Excessively high thresholds, it said, would allow unhealthy products to escape scrutiny, leaving consumers unknowingly exposed to harmful levels of sugar, saturated fat and salt, while excessively low thresholds could result in nearly all packaged foods carrying warnings, eventually desensitising consumers and inducing “label fatigue”.

The court also prescribed changes to the design of the warning labels, directing the FSSAI to provide a separate red hexagon for each nutrient of concern, with a standardised pictorial representation accompanied by the words “HIGH FAT”, “HIGH SUGAR” or “HIGH SALT”.
Products exceeding the thresholds for multiple nutrients would thus have to carry distinct warnings for each.
Drawing on international practices, the Bench directed that each hexagon occupy a minimum of 4% to 5% of the package’s principal display panel, unless reasons exist for departing from this standard.

“The FSSAI shall also prescribe the font size of the text within each hexagon such that it is prominent, conspicuous and readily legible to consumers when viewed together with the pictorial representation of each nutrient-of-concern under normal conditions of purchase and use,” the Bench said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Must Not Remain A Court Of Privileged Few : CJI Surya Kant On Constitution Day
stories.title: Supreme Court Must Not Remain A Court Of Privileged Few : CJI Surya Kant On Constitution Day
stories.summary: "We are on a continuous mission to ensure that no citizen ever finds the doors of justice closed," the CJI said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: "We are on a continuous mission to ensure that no citizen ever finds the doors of justice closed," the CJI said.

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Thursday (November 26) said the Supreme Court must continue working towards ensuring that justice reaches every citizen, acknowledging that the institution was, at one time, seen as a court of the privileged and that access to it could depend on who sought a hearing rather than the urgency of the matter.
In order to dismantle barriers to access to justice, the CJI highlighted listing reforms such as automatic listing of fresh matters are listed without lawyers having to seek dates in court.
Cases concerning personal liberty or urgent interim relief are required to reach a bench within two working days, he said.

The Court has also identified litigants who may face greater barriers in accessing justice, including persons with disabilities, acid attack survivors, senior citizens above 80 years of age, people below the poverty line and litigants approaching the Court through legal aid.
Their cases receive priority listing, he said.

The CJI said that such priorities are based on criteria announced in advance and applied uniformly, ensuring that case listing follows a transparent and consistent pattern without undue favour to anyone.

Addressing the Supreme Court's Constitution Day celebrations, the CJI said the Constitution was conceived not as a charter of advantages for a fortunate few, but as a covenant of justice with every citizen.

Recalling the words of Constituent Assembly member Mithi Hansa Mehta, who had said that women sought social, economic and political justice rather than privileges, the CJI said that the distinction between privilege and justice lay at the heart of the Constitution.
He likened the Supreme Court's jurisprudence to a Pashmina shawl, saying that thousands of judgments, patiently laid together, had helped shelter the Republic.
However, he pointed out that even a precious shawl could protect only those who could afford to wrap it around themselves.
Thus, he said, the Court must reflect on whether justice had reached everyone it was intended for.

stories.headline: Supreme Court orders junk food warning labels, with a separate red flag each for sugar, salt and fat
stories.title: Supreme Court orders junk food warning labels, with a separate red flag each for sugar, salt and fat
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday ordered stark warning labels on packaged foods high in sugar, salt or fat, with a separate hexagon flagging each nutrient, as it rejected a watered-down version of the scheme as something that would "undermine the very objective" of the exercise.

Each nutrient must get "a separate hexagon", carrying the words "High Fat", "High Sugar" or "High Salt" with a matching pictogram, "rather than a single combined hexagon", the court said, asking the rules to come into force within a four-month timeline proposed by the food regulator.
Companies will then get a 365-day transition period.

In a 131-page judgment, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to fix design and threshold flaws in its draft warning-label scheme.
It also told the regulator to hold to its own timeline for bringing the rules into force.
The ruling will impact everything from chips and biscuits to fizzy drinks.

"A consumer in India is entitled to no less protection, and no less information, than a consumer in the United States or the United Kingdom," the court said, calling reports of differing practices by global companies "deeply troubling" if true.
It named no company and urged multinationals to adopt uniform standards across countries.
The FSSAI had proposed a single red hexagon carrying the words "High Sugar", "High Saturated Fat" and "High Salt".
The court said that would not work.
It ordered a separate hexagon for each nutrient, each with its own pictogram and the words "High Fat", "High Sugar" or "High Salt".
It said the design should let a shopper see at a glance that a product is high in all three, without parsing text.

stories.headline: Rahul Madan takes charge as IBBI Chairperson
stories.title: Rahul Madan takes charge as IBBI Chairperson
stories.summary: He has over 24 years career in the banking and financial services sector, including stints at the State Bank of India, Kotak Mahindra Bank and ICICI Bank
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'takes charge' in title weight 40
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) on Thursday said Rahul Madan has taken charge as the Chairperson.
Madan - a chartered accountant, cost and management accountant and qualified insolvency professional - replaces Ravi Mital, who retired from the post in September.
IBBI Whole Time Member Jayanti Prasad was holding the additional charge of Chairperson in the interim.
In a release, IBBI said Madan took charge as the Chairperson on November 25.
Prior to the new role, Madan served as the Managing Director of the Indian Institute of Insolvency Professionals of ICAI (IIIPI) for over six years.
He has over 24 years career in the banking and financial services sector, including stints at the State Bank of India, Kotak Mahindra Bank and ICICI Bank.

According to the release, he has worked in diverse areas, including corporate banking, credit and risk management, investment banking, debt advisory, structured finance and institutional wealth management.
IBBI is a key institution in implementation of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC).
